On September 4, IFA 2026 will open at the Berlin Exhibition Center in Germany. As one of the world's largest consumer electronics and home appliance trade shows, IFA attracts over 1,900 exhibitors showcasing cutting-edge technologies and products ranging from robotics, AI, and smart homes to flying cars. At the pre-show warm-up event, IFA CEO Leif Lindner predicted that AI would be deeply embedded throughout this year's show. He noted that previous IFAs had dedicated AI zones to accommodate related companies and products, but today AI has evolved from a niche category into the infrastructure underpinning the entire consumer electronics industry, integrating into nearly every product segment.

Anker has also recognized this transformation AI is bringing to the consumer electronics industry. On September 3, ahead of the official opening of IFA, Anker held a global press conference announcing that it would consolidate its five brands—Anker, Anker SOLIX, eufy, eufyMake, and soundcore—under the single "Anker" brand. This brand strategy upgrade aligns with the broader industry trend: as AI, on-device computing, robotics, and IoT technologies advance, category boundaries are becoming increasingly blurred. This is not just an internal brand architecture integration for Anker, but also a move to significantly reduce consumers' cognitive load—users will only need to recognize one Anker brand to enjoy a seamless intelligent experience throughout their journey. "In an era where categories were independent, building category brands made sense. But today, a new era has arrived."

En el acto de presentación de la feria, el consejero delegado de la IFA, Leif Lindner, anticipó que la IA impregnará este año la esencia misma de la feria. Señaló que en ediciones anteriores la IFA contaba con una zona exclusiva de IA para albergar a las empresas y productos de este ámbito; sin embargo, hoy la IA ha pasado de ser una categoría específica a convertirse en la infraestructura que sustenta todo el sector de la electrónica de consumo, integrándose en prácticamente todas las categorías.

excerpt_i18n.en: In 2018, Wang Yansen was still an undergraduate working on generative dialogue. At the time, computer vision was all the rage, and the Transformer wave was just beginning. When he told people he was building "a chatbot that can chat," they would often nod politely, their expressions saying, "Very cutting-edge, but so what?" At academic exchange events, the person next to him would always ask: "What can a chatbot bring? What can it change?" He tried to explain "emotional companionship," but faced with more skepticism, even he couldn't articulate it clearly. That confusion carried over to the SenseTime Scholarship interview—at that point he wasn't quite sure how to explain it in a way that sounded convincing either. But that year, he received the scholarship notification. The ¥20,000 prize was substantial, practical support for an undergraduate at the time. More importantly, the recognition from a top AI institution instilled confidence in him at his most wavering moment. Four years later, ChatGPT exploded, and generative AI began gradually entering households worldwide. Wang Yansen and those who walked the same path had their once-lonely explorations validated by time. Today, he works at Microsoft Research Asia (Shanghai). Recalling this in a conversation with Leiphone's AI Technology Review, he said: "The process of doing research can be lonely, but you know that at that crossroads, someone lit a lamp for you.
